g.text: Figure 2
Item-level proportional-odds model of outrage tone
The five indicators use the coding and reference categories in Figure 1.
Five 0/1 indicators, in this order
X = [I(polsys=2), I(polsys=3), I(socdiv=2), I(mediatype=2), I(mediatype=3)]
Order: mixed, majoritarian, contested, website, newspaper
Codes above are analytical codes. Bases are consensus, stable secularism and blogs.
eta_i = X_i beta1
Five fixed slopes
No separate free intercept or random effects
Four ordered cutpoints
Slopes common across all four thresholds
Item tone: archive 1-5 is recoded to 0-4
logit Pr(tone_i > k) = eta_i - c_k, k = 0,1,2,3
Pr(tone_i = k) = F(c_k - eta_i) - F(c_(k-1) - eta_i), F = logistic CDF
Five ordered categories, with outer cutpoints at minus/plus infinity
N = 1700 news items. The reference-row copy of tone is not a separate M1 sample.
Unweighted maximum likelihood, observed information, normal 95% Wald intervals.
No random effects, centering, interactions, mediation, priors or imputation.
C1 retains the original assumption diagnostics, C2 the original alternative links, P1 the probabilities.
Unmeasured compromise, identity boundaries and editorial gatekeeping are proposed mechanisms.
They are not estimated mediators in M1, M2 or M3.
Input: data/original/MedCon_Civility_item.dta, with item likelihood independence assumed.
Note. Original AI-assisted reconstruction from author code, not a copied published figure. Student review pending.
